title: Joss and the Glitter Calamity
markdown:
Moonlight made dust motes into a private weather system over Northwood Academy’s workshop. Joss Button stood at the bench with confidence like a sail in too much wind. Waffles, a wiry terrier, quivered on the edge of a yodel. Tonight, Joss had declared, was the night.

He wanted the hush of awe. Under it sat the older fear: being seen as a fraud. His hands shook on a lever.

“Witness the birth of the Auto-Assembler 3000.” He flicked a switch. Clicks, then a shudder, then the machine taking itself apart. Gears fled. Springs jumped like grasshoppers. Glitter exploded, sticky, iridescent, personal. Clockwork birds complained. Triumph had become the Great Kinetic Calamity.

He scrambled for schematics that now looked foreign. “Minor setback.” He navigated a toppling stack, glitter in his eyebrows, tasting like regret. The main conduit sparked at oily rags. Fleeing suggested itself.

His foot found a forgotten case. Inside, a crude counterweight: unfussy, stable, a humble anchor. To quiet the conduit he needed its mass. To place it he had to dump tension from the main springs.

Ozone. Waffles, sensing theatre, detonated a series of yips. “Quiet,” Joss hissed, which the terrier took as accompaniment. He yanked the releases. The frame groaned. For a breath the machine sagged inward. He shoved the counterweight onto the sparking wires. They went dark. Metal shavings rained onto glittered shoulders.

He dismantled the counterweight and left the mangled Assembler to its fate. Waffles trotted after him to his own bench, the heavy simple thing in his arms.

Morning: no explosions. Interlocking gears, held by the counterweight, boring as competence. A few students drifted over because nothing was on fire. Joss, without pronouncements, showed how steady pressure kept the line true. A cracked bell, lightning-scarred, hung on a hook. When he nudged the rig it gave one low dong, a quiet truth. He smiled without forcing it. The disaster had not delivered applause. It had delivered a hum he could live with.
characters: Joss Button (overconfident map-reader with hidden good judgement who is trying very hard to seem sensible), Waffles (a small dog who always chooses the loudest possible moment)
audience: teenagers aged 13-15, high-quality story for confident readers
